打车去高铁站，点了特惠快车。上了车，司机大哥对着手机跟他的兄弟骂骂咧咧，说跑了半上午就挣100块。

我问说师傅你到账多少钱，对了一下发现平台抽走25%。师傅说这还算少的，最高要抽 29%。

我说师傅我们也不容易。随之我虚构了一个老板，说自己过得也很惨，天天加班，工资还低。

果然一听对方也过得不好，大哥打开了话匣子。说前个月坚决不开特惠，一天只能挣200。上个月开始开特惠，一天能挣400，但是从早开到晚，十几个小时不休息。

我说我们也是啊，根本没有双休，累得要死要活，到手就一点钱。

大哥眉头眼见着舒展了，跟我说起了自己的事，说每天出门带着100块钱，顶当天的吃喝，花销，给车充电。给我讲了早上跟媳妇要钱的故事。

说着说着说俩人还没结婚，但是钱已经都给媳妇实际上还是对象管了，又说媳妇挣得也多但花得更多，言语间是带着甜蜜的抱怨。

我说这还不是你稀罕人家吗？师傅说对，我俩是一小区的，她是我同学的妹妹。我说你可以啊。他马上说啊对，虽说兔子不吃窝边草，但是我看上的人必须拿下。

小吹一牛，我下车的时候，师傅高高兴兴的走了。

我愿意让大家心情不错，哪怕是偶然遇到的人。

对于老百姓，快车和特惠快车体验、速度，完全一样，特惠快车还便宜20块钱，快车和特惠当然选特惠。

平台照此逻辑给司机派单，快车打的人少，当然司机的单少。

平台就是赌你不开特惠你就接不到单，你不想干有的是人干。

但我总觉得自己也参与了这场平台和司机的博弈，帮着平台欺压每天奔走在路上的司机。

干实业的老板愁着年底给工人发工资，干互联网的听闻今年也没好到哪去。

更多人下岗，更多人开滴滴，更多的不开特惠，你就接不到单。

在传统市场上，需求和交易效率，没有任何变化。

冗余、利润，都去哪了呢？

很幸运，我所谓的跟上了时代，我勇立潮头，我在创造，我在桌上，没被淘汰。

好消息我们吃饱穿暖了，但毫无进展地度过时间，可能是时代里的多数。

无它。开心快乐，锻炼身体！切记。

text: just quick retraction of my (deleted) post that I've not been using AI. after being traumatized by GPT 5.5 fucking up, Fable being withdrawn, and Opus 4.8 being depressingly dumb (relatively), I spent some days coding manually and I made a lot of progress. that said, I over-compensated. pure manual coding is not faster than using AI. it is faster than using AI poorly. like everything, there is a balance where you use it responsibly: audits, well specified refactors, sanity checks... where you can extract a lot of value. my mistake was letting codex edit a lot of code unsupervised without really reading its output. that's clearly my own fault for using it poorly and Bend's delay is attributable to it. it is a new powerful tech. I think not using it is a mistake, but using it too aggressively is a mistake too. I've been using AI carefully and doing things way slower now, taking the time needed to assert each added functionality is correct, well written, and well understood, before moving to the next, and, by doing so, things are actually moving faster, because progress only moves forward, never backward - which happens a lot when you let AI unsupervised. I'm halfway through. Bend2 has 50% of the pre-rewrite features, except the code is now beautiful and extremely robust. this is not adding anything it didn't have, I'm just ensuring the codebase mets my own quality standards

I've been using AI carefully and doing things way slower now, taking the time needed to assert each added functionality is correct, well written, and well understood, before moving to the next, and, by doing so, things are actually moving faster, because progress only moves forward, never backward - which happens a lot when you let AI unsupervised. I'm halfway through. Bend2 has 50% of the pre-rewrite features, except the code is now beautiful and extremely robust. this is not adding anything it didn't have, I'm just ensuring the codebase mets my own quality standards

text:
我说实话，哈工大院士班出来以后，对于绝大多数高考600分（赋分制省份640分）以上的学生来说，绝对是致命一击。

就是说，在中国目前的学制下，7年才能本科+硕士毕业，11年才能本硕博毕业，

然而哈工大院士班的同学，6年直接本硕博全部拿到，直接毕业，AI、航院控制自动化、电子、材料四选一，

这种事情大概相当于，你天天37度上晚自习，你一毕业了，学校装了空调，并且晚自习人人免费酸梅汤、免费炸鸡腿无限供应。

直接成了他妈时代的眼泪了。

哪怕是清华大学的毕业生，你回忆你和你们班劝退专业傻逼们一起卷了整整4年GPA，考托福，考GRE，录取美国名校PhD，五年完成qualify，发paper，做一两期postdoc，完完全全在浪费人生。

再看哈工大院士班，哪怕是GPA垫底25%，也能6年材料博士毕业，也能直接躺进宁德时代拿年薪80万（对，宁德时代给new grad PhD尤其是target school就是这个数字），

完完全全不低于字节和智谱、moonshot这个档次的7年制本硕毕业的工资。

我说实话，哈工大当年4系无数人，是贴着清华分数线考进来的，4系航院自动化到今天都是哈工大第一王牌专业，压久负盛名中国NLP小斯坦福的哈工大3系计算机一头，

然而我们班同学们今天回忆这件事，一定是又高兴又怅然若失。

现在的孩子们是真幸运，迎来了哈工大院士班这种6年制本博连读，这就是他妈的时代，这就是他妈的未来可期。

A lack of competition eventually becomes a lack of competitiveness.

text:
时间线上有大量的智谱glm5.2 的讨论，结合最近跟几个投资方聊天，他们给出的观点非常粗暴，

说个有意思的事，国内 AI 应用软件，在市场上是没人愿意投的，原因很简单，大模型们版本迭代，就可能把一个细分领域的 AI软件内化迭代，甚至是一个 skill 就能搞定你几十人的团队的产品，靠信息差挣点小钱还行，靠资本基本上没戏了。

说回，GLM-5.2，它不是新模型，而是同一模型家族的优化版本。想象一下：GLM-5.1是一辆标准版汽车，GLM-5.2是同一辆车但调校了发动机和变速箱，让它跑得更快更省油，但底盘和车身没变。性能提升来自强化学习（让模型在试错中学习）和训练后优化（微调模型输出），而不是堆更多参数。结果是：成本基本不变，但输出质量更高，客户愿意为更好的任务完成率、更少的重试、更高价值的用例（编码、代理、企业工作流自动化、长上下文任务）支付更多。

我看讨论最少但是最需要理清的一件事，到底 glm 是国产芯片训练还是靠美国芯片？

4 个月前，昇腾0day支持智谱GLM-5，744B模型单机高效推理，GLM 5.2 Day0，也是完成全系列国产算力芯片适配，这里有没有英伟达芯片参与的水分，必然是有的，但是整体是国产配比更高一些。

将于8月发布GLM-5.5 大模型，可能还会颠覆中国大模型在世界的影响力，可能是>1T参数模型。

摩根大通将智谱AI目标价从1400港元上调至1800港元，维持增持评级。基于30倍2030年市盈率，15% WACC折现。

text:
别赌球了，尤其是世界杯。

随着2026美加墨世界杯小组赛进入白热化，不少人已经开始买两手、重仓绝杀。

今天我们不谈道德，只讲概率、博弈论，以及本届世界杯已经出现的真实情况。

假设一场势均力敌的比赛，真实概率是50-50，公平赔率应该是2.0。但实际盘口你拿到的往往是1.85~1.90。
这中间消失的0.1~0.15，就是庄家的Margin，通常在5%~8%之间。

根据大数法则，单场可能靠运气赢，但只要持续投注，随着次数增加，你的收益率会不可避免地向-抽水率收敛。
玩得越多，亏得越稳。这是数学问题。

今年扩军到48队、12个小组，比赛数量大幅增加，冷门和平局的随机性也随之上升。你自以为掌握的规律，在更多变量面前，期望值会进一步恶化。

庄家从来不是在跟你赌谁赢球。

他们通过实时调整盘口和水位，让两边资金尽量平衡，自己稳吃抽水。无论场上结果如何，庄家已经通过对冲锁定了利润。

零和博弈？
别搞笑了，这是负和博弈。
整个赌徒群体的钱在不断被平台抽走。你想长期从这个系统里赚钱，难度远超你想象。

很多人看到西班牙0-0佛得角、巴西1-1摩洛哥、葡萄牙1-1刚果、比利时被埃及逼平等结果，就立刻喊有剧本。

这是典型的模式识别错误。

在扩军后的世界杯，小组赛出现大量冷门和平局是完全正常的：

很多弱队防守反击打得极好
强队轮换、疲劳、热适应问题
低比分运动本身方差就极大

把随机性归因于全球剧本，这很危险 。

因为当你相信有剧本时，你会更愿意下重注、追损、相信自己能看穿剧本。结果就是输得更快更惨。
真正有剧本的比赛如果存在，也只会让普通赌徒更难盈利，而不是更容易。

长期来看，95%以上的体育赌徒是亏损的。
即使你有一定分析能力，抽水，方差，信息不对称，依然会把大多数人慢慢磨死。

所以，珍爱生命财产，远离赌球。

text:
Google 开始试点让软件工程候选人在部分面试环节使用 Gemini。

过去几年有个很奇怪的现象：

工作中要求你会用 AI。

面试中要求你别用 AI。

很多工程师每天都在用 Claude、Gemini、Codex、Cursor。

结果面试时却还在手写算法题。

Google 这次其实是在承认一个现实：

软件工程师的核心能力，正在从「写代码」变成「利用 AI 构建软件」。

未来的面试，考的可能不再是谁记得更多 API。

而是谁更会提问、更会验证、更会 Debug、更会驾驭 AI。

问题来了：

如果 AI 可以参与面试，

LeetCode 还有存在的必要吗？

text:
马克•莱文估计要被川普臭骂了。

😂😀✌️

这家伙是川普和内塔尼亚胡共同的好朋友。

不过，自从川普搞出美伊谅解备忘录以后，他几乎天天抱怨川普，这次是直接攻击川普和川普政府了。

他在自己的节目里这样说：

“请停止诋毁、中伤、欺凌以色列这个小国。

停止讨好伊朗，不要尝试告诉我们，伊朗的敌对政权现在更加理性、更加温和。就在几个月前，他们屠杀了5万人。

如果他们今天拥有核导弹，他们会像我还活着一样确凿无疑地将其发射到我们国家。我不知道现在这是怎么回事。”

……

他这是明目张胆攻击川普政府欺负以色列和讨好伊朗。

川普能饶得了他？

坐等川普发文开骂。

😂😂😂😀😀😀✌️✌️✌️

text:
足球最适合揭穿三个谎言：

第一个谎言是“只要国家重视，就能办成事”。
中国足球恰恰是国家高度重视之后，仍然长期失败的案例。

第二个谎言是“集中力量办大事一定有效”。
足球不是修桥、修路、建高铁。它需要基层自发、长期竞争、俱乐部自治、青训耐心、教练专业。权力越想直接控制，越容易破坏足球规律。

第三个谎言是“中国人不行”。
日本、韩国已经证明东亚人可以踢好足球。中国足球失败不是民族失败，而是制度失败。

这三个谎言一旦被拆开，很多人就会自然联想到教育、医疗、电影、出版、互联网、民营经济、大学科研：是不是很多领域也是一样？不是中国人没能力，而是制度把人的能力压住了。

result.text:
I used to be a die-hard Claude Code user.

Codex has won me over because:

→ GPT-5.5 is excellent
→ Fast mode + generous limits = more reps
→ Little touches like steering, auto remote control on phone, etc

But most of all Codex's browser and computer use capabilities are simply goated. I built so many workflows relying on those two things alone instead of hunting for APIs.

I still use Claude Code too. The app seems to be getting better and the design and frontend capability of Opus is still much better than GPT. Whenever Fable comes back that's another reason to go back.

Honestly, I hope these two compete forever and other players (Cursor/Grok, Gemini, etc) all stay competitive.

This way the builder keeps winning 🙂

别再问「本地 Qwen 能不能替代 Claude opus」了，这个问题本身就问偏了。

Alex Ellis 这篇文章值得我们关注：他花了一万多美元搭本地 AI，用 Qwen 做客户支持、诊断分析、代码库阅读和 licence 数据检查，甚至一次帮公司追回了足够覆盖显卡成本的收入。

但他也说得很直白：本地模型还扛不住 Claude / Codex 那种长时间无人监督的复杂开发任务。它会循环、幻觉、读错文件、跑偏，尤其在量化和长上下文场景里更明显。

所以本地 AI 的价值，不在于变成一个便宜版 Opus。

它更像一把专用工具：适合处理敏感数据，适合固定成本的大量分析，适合不想把客户资料丢进云端的场景。

云端模型像外科医生，强、贵、可靠；本地模型像车库里的工具台，没那么聪明，但胜在可控、私密、随叫随到。

真正成熟的 AI 工作流，可能不会只押一种模型。

该用 Opus 的时候用 Opus，该用本地模型的时候用本地模型。

关键不是「谁更强」，而是你有没有把不同工具放到正确的位置。

text:
LLM 每一轮迭代，都会让一批创业者丢掉生意。今天跟一位朋友聊，他说模型越强，他却越兴奋。

他是做硬件集成解决方案的，前十年在工厂摸爬滚打，2023 年 AI 爆发后开始跟着 waytoagi 社区沉浸式学习，将 AI 能力转换成生产力，然后将经验复制到工厂生产场景，写 prompt，建 workflow，也捏 agent，认识了很多工厂老板。

两年下来，最大的感受是，再好用的提示词和工作流，都会随着大模型能力的提升成为历史的遗迹。这也一度让他产生焦虑。

今年年初，他把投入的方向做了一些调整。Coding agent 的能力跃迁，让 AI 可以做好大量繁琐工作的拆解了，例如可以把工厂的需求拆解成更具体的电路问题和软件设计问题，将复杂的电路集成问题拆解成可单元化合成的简单问题。凭借着对硬件领域的认知和人脉关系，他开始从咨询顾问转型为硬件集成方，除了做方案供给，也把软硬件实现环节给承接了下来。

在能力打磨阶段，一方面承接市场各类个性化定制需求，一对一客服，另一方面线下跑工厂，帮助工厂完成 AI 转型和升级。过程中，把对 AI 的理解附加到硬件产品上，又把对硬件的理解融入到AI 的交互体验中，逐步积累了深厚的技术壁垒和认知壁垒。

过去半年，他几乎每天只睡四个小时。为了解决某个硬件集成或设计问题，会去了解每个元件的工作原理，做好参数调试，以及供应商对比，在实战中沉淀和优化了丰富的元件知识库，也与大量硬件供应商建立信任关系，很快就逐渐形成了自己的集成方案优势、价格优势和服务体验优势。

他说这些都是脏活苦活累活，很多人不愿意下场，愿意下场的人又不懂 AI，也就没办法将沉淀的知识转换成有效生产力。

在做生意方面，也是务实的风格。遇到了好的硬件想法和创意，他并没有直接下场实现，而是把利润让给合适工厂，跟工厂一起打磨更顺畅的合作模式，同时也为自己建设更全面的硬件调试能力，以此来构建更持久、更健康的生态合作环境。

跟这个朋友的沟通，让我感受到，1）无论是数字时代还是智能时代，都需要下苦功夫，没有捷径可走；2）行业 know-how 就是最强护城河，充分发挥自己的领域优势，结合 AI 把人解决起来最难、最痛苦的问题搞定，前面就是曙光；3）做生意，三分利七分情，生态好了，自己才会更好。

美国知名保守派媒体人塔克·卡尔森，这位川普曾经的密友针对美国和伊朗签署的备忘录，最近在他的播客节目中说，“你们可能总会幻想，美国霸权某一天走向终结，最可能会发生在与另一大国的剧烈冲突中……比如与中国就台湾问题爆发冲突。”“可你们大概想不到，美国帝国的终结，会发生在一场持续一百多天的冲突中。而对手，竟是一个经济规模排在全球34位的波斯湾小国，一个叫伊朗的国家。”

这个看法与我不谋而合，我5月在FT发文，标题就是“美伊战争，或许是美国霸权终结的开始”。卡尔森其实比我看得还严重，我加了一个定语“或许”，并且认为只是开始，霸权的完全终结有一个长过程，中间或许还会出现中兴，但看他的意思，美国霸权是已经终结了。

text:
At 3pm today I was in Menlo Park and debating heading to SF to work out of a cafe. Then I remembered that there's literally no great cafes to work out of in SF that are open past 5pm. Maybe some meh ones open until 6pm, but def nothing worth the drive. Ironic given that SF is supposed to be the place for building startups.

If you like working out of cafes, SF is surprisingly bad for it. Most cafes are cute little spots that close 3-5pm and barely have seating. I haven't found a single great cafe that combines modern design, ample seating, and remains open past 5pm. Actually I have yet to find a single cafe that even just checks those first two boxes.

The #1 city in the world for working out of cafes is Seoul, and its surrounding suburbs. You could be in a random suburb of Seoul, and within 15 minutes walking distance there will be a quality work cafe with tasteful modern design, ample seating, thriving co-working space vibes, and open 24/7. There are even 24/7 cafes with zero employees - something that could never exist in the U.S.

I was in Tokyo last week and saw the most beautiful and aesthetic co-working space I've ever seen where you can rent by the hour or day, attached to one of the nicest bookstores I've ever seen, two more hip and stylish cafes, all in a beautiful building and beautiful area. A 15 minute walk away was the nicest Starbucks Reserve I've ever seen, with 4 floors. These kind of places don't exist in the U.S, and definitely don't exist in SF. 

Ironically, Tokyo and Seoul are probably better places to build a startup if you're just working from your laptop, don't have an office and prefer working out of cafes to holing up in your apartment all day in your pajamas, don't need to beg rich people for funding, and don't care about networking.

Anyways I ended up driving 10 mins to Mountain View to work out of the only cafe I know here with ample seating, modern design, and open till 6pm. Of course it has nothing on what I saw in Asia though (attached photos are from Tokyo)

- Sortie très probable le jeudi 25 juin.
- Environ 5× moins cher que Fable 5
- Jusqu'à 2M de tokens en fenêtre de contexte
- Date limite de connaissances : décembre 2025 (les versions précédentes avaient 08/2025).
- Effort de raisonnement (« Juice Value ») augmenté à 960 (contre 768 sur GPT-5.5).
- Il surpasse Fable sur les workflows de codage agentique
- La vision et la réplication de concepts à partir d'images sont bien meilleures (il peut copier les designs en site web)
- La génération de SVG, en particulier les SVG 3D et statiques, est excellente et peut surpasser Fable 5.
- Génération frontend s'est améliorée.
- Génération de jeux est plus stable avec moins de glitchs visuels.
- Support Playwright est intégré à ChatGPT.

La semaine prochaine va être très cool !

text:
Colombian startups collectively raised US$46.6 million this week alone 🇨🇴

Major rounds include:

> Telepatía AI (@Nicobot01 ): US$33 million Series A round
> El Dorado (@eldoradoio , @stablecoing ): US$9 million Series A round
> Braven: US$4.6 million Seed round

Congratulations to the founding teams for putting Colombia in the global startup spotlight and building such cool companies.

Two interesting facts stand out to me.

a) Early-stage is not dead. Since the beginning of the year, many have complained that funding was going only toward later stages.

This trend has reversed this quarter, and the Colombian ecosystem is now leading the charge.

b) There's a healthy diversification of sectors being funded, with the biggest round going to a HealthTech, followed by a FinTech and an InsurTech.

A pretty clear picture of the hot sectors right now in the region.

A special mention to neighboring startup Karta (US-Ecuador @Freddyjuez ) for its US$15 million Series A round and $125M warehouse facility as well!

text:
🇺🇸TODAY IN AMERICAN HISTORY🇺🇸
June 21, 1867, at Cimarron Crossing, Kansas, Cheyenne warriors attacked a wagon train that included Bishop Jean-Baptiste Lamy (future Archbishop of Santa Fe).

Lamy was traveling with a large religious party (roughly a dozen priests and a dozen nuns) when the night raid struck. Like many raids on the Santa Fe Trail during this period, the main goal was stealing livestock rather than killing people. 

The Cheyenne made off with about 80 animals. Casualties among the travelers were minimal, and because the party was relatively close to settled areas, they were never in danger of being stranded.

Still, the attack on a Catholic bishop and his entourage still caused a significant stir back East.

text:
在故乡的夜色里，我常常想起那些沉默的老人。

儿女有了出息，远走异国，便等于不曾生养；去了大都会，也只剩半个；唯有留在身边的，虽穷困些，却还算有个依靠。这话初听极端，细想却如一把钝刀，慢慢割进心底，叫人久久不能言语。

世人总以为，孩子越聪明、越有本事，自己晚景便越安乐。殊不知，越是优秀的苗子，越发长得远。出了国的，隔着时差与重洋；进了城的，被事务所与生计牢牢缚住；只有那不争气的，才真正在生活里陪着你。如此一来，世上便出现了一桩极荒谬的景象：儿女越有出息，父母越发孤单。

这原是极现实的道理。人到后半生，所求便变了。少年时要的是天地，要的是前程；到得垂暮，所要的不过是——有人能说说话，有人能在病榻边递一口水，有人能在半夜惊醒时，推门进来点一盏灯。

钱能买来药，却买不来那守在走廊里的身影；电话能传声，却填不满屋子里那一片死寂。一个人在医院的长椅上枯坐，与有人陪着，是两样完全不同的人生。

前些时，网上流传一张“A4纸人生”。把七十五年折成九百个月，若一年只见父母一面，剩下的光阴便只剩薄薄十几格。白纸黑线，看似轻飘飘，细看却叫人胸口发闷。

我们一生都在奔走，奔向更远、更亮堂的地方，以为那是“更好”。却不曾留意：我们每向前一步，父母便向孤独深处退一步。我们走得越远，他们的日子便越窄，越冷。

所以，诸位在外漂泊的，若还有一丝空闲，便打一个电话吧；若还有一口气力，便发一段视频吧；若还有可能，便多回几次家，哪怕只坐一坐，陪他们晒晒太阳，说几句闲话。

人生固然漫长，可真正能陪父母的光阴，其实少得可怜。待到只剩一抔黄土、一缕回忆时，才忽然醒悟：原来那最该走的一段路，我们竟缺席了。

这世间，最锋利的不是刀，而是迟来的悔。

What is Quantised Inertia (QI)?
Mike McCulloch (a physicist and author) has been developing Quantised Inertia (also called MiHsC in earlier papers) since 2007. It's an alternative model of inertia based on the idea that:
Inertia arises from Unruh radiation (quantum vacuum fluctuations seen by accelerating objects).
This radiation is modified ("quantised") by horizons, especially the Hubble horizon on cosmic scales.
The theory aims to explain several longstanding puzzles without invoking dark matter or dark energy, and it predicts new effects like propellantless thrust from certain devices (e.g., asymmetric capacitors or cavities).
Key Claims in the Video (from description + summary)
McCulloch lists supporting observations across scales, most tied to his peer-reviewed papers:
Cosmic scales: Cosmic acceleration (~2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s²), flatness of the universe, low-ℓ CMB anomaly, Hubble tension.
Galactic scales: Galaxy rotation curves, wide binary star orbits, Proxima Centauri’s motion (by reducing inertial mass at low accelerations).
Solar system/lab anomalies: Pioneer anomaly, flyby anomalies, variations in measured G, relativistic jets.
Smaller scales / lab experiments: Cold fusion/LENR claims, Tajmar’s spinning discs, asymmetric cavity thrust, capacitor effects, Podkletnov’s gravity claims, and EM Drive-like thrust in conical cavities.
He also derives G from the theory and discusses implications for time and the EPR paradox.
He emphasizes 20+ years of publications and that many predictions match data without free parameters or "dark" stuff.<grok:render card_id="1f232a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render>
Broader Context
QI is controversial and not part of mainstream physics. It modifies the standard understanding of inertia in a way that challenges general relativity and the ΛCDM model at certain scales. Critics argue it lacks rigorous derivation in some areas or conflicts with established experiments, while supporters (including McCulloch) point to its predictive successes on anomalies that standard models struggle with.
There was DARPA funding (~$1.3M in 2018) for related experiments, and McCulloch continues publishing (including recent work on Proxima Centauri and Jupiter-mass binary objects seen by JWST). He maintains a blog at physicsfromtheedge.blogspot.com and a site at quantizedinertia.com.
A reply in the thread mentions a possible connection to entanglement as angular momentum and string theory potentially recreating similar ideas.

items.message:
**This X post** from Mike McCulloch (@memcculloch) is him sharing his own new YouTube video:

> **"The Reasons I Am So Confident About Quantised Inertia"**  
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CA_lZgrmcUk

**Posted today** (June 21, 2026) with low initial engagement (26 views, 6 likes at the time of checking). The video is short (~6.5 minutes) and he describes it as listing "many observations, both astrophysical and lab-based, that support quantised inertia" along with references.

### What is Quantised Inertia (QI)?
Mike McCulloch (a physicist and author) has been developing **Quantised Inertia** (also called MiHsC in earlier papers) since 2007. It's an alternative model of **inertia** based on the idea that:

- Inertia arises from Unruh radiation (quantum vacuum fluctuations seen by accelerating objects).
- This radiation is modified ("quantised") by horizons, especially the Hubble horizon on cosmic scales.

The theory aims to explain several longstanding puzzles **without** invoking dark matter or dark energy, and it predicts new effects like propellantless thrust from certain devices (e.g., asymmetric capacitors or cavities).

### Key Claims in the Video (from description + summary)
McCulloch lists supporting observations across scales, most tied to his peer-reviewed papers:

- **Cosmic scales**: Cosmic acceleration (~2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s²), flatness of the universe, low-ℓ CMB anomaly, Hubble tension.
- **Galactic scales**: Galaxy rotation curves, wide binary star orbits, Proxima Centauri’s motion (by reducing inertial mass at low accelerations).
- **Solar system/lab anomalies**: Pioneer anomaly, flyby anomalies, variations in measured G, relativistic jets.
- **Smaller scales / lab experiments**: Cold fusion/LENR claims, Tajmar’s spinning discs, asymmetric cavity thrust, capacitor effects, Podkletnov’s gravity claims, and EM Drive-like thrust in conical cavities.
- He also derives G from the theory and discusses implications for time and the EPR paradox.

He emphasizes 20+ years of publications and that many predictions match data without free parameters or "dark" stuff.

### Broader Context
QI is **controversial and not part of mainstream physics**. It modifies the standard understanding of inertia in a way that challenges general relativity and the ΛCDM model at certain scales. Critics argue it lacks rigorous derivation in some areas or conflicts with established experiments, while supporters (including McCulloch) point to its predictive successes on anomalies that standard models struggle with.

There was DARPA funding (~$1.3M in 2018) for related experiments, and McCulloch continues publishing (including recent work on Proxima Centauri and Jupiter-mass binary objects seen by JWST). He maintains a blog at physicsfromtheedge.blogspot.com and a site at quantizedinertia.com.

A reply in the thread mentions a possible connection to entanglement as angular momentum and string theory potentially recreating similar ideas.

If you want:
- A deeper dive into any specific claim from the video
- Links to his key papers
- My take on the strengths/weaknesses of QI as an alternative theory
- Or anything else related

Just let me know! It's an interesting, ambitious attempt to rethink fundamentals from the quantum vacuum outward.

text:
Starry-eyed “abundance” talk is just a failure to identify the next bottleneck.

Steam commoditized mechanical effort, the internet commoditized information distribution, and so on. Robotics may commoditize certain broad swaths of labor, but production is constrained by the scarcest complementary input, not the most abundant one. As the price of labor approaches ~zero, economic rents will shift: to energy, land, compute, raw materials, coordination, and institutional constraints.

公开开源的库是剥离了那个内部的 「context 」上下文，以及内部使用的一些 Skill 。 

所以我们看到的当前库是没有任何 AI Coding 痕迹。 

但公开库的 Docs 非常专业和系统，我想这是给外部贡献者准备的，包括外部 AI Agent 。

text:
Comparison of bee products based on assays of antioxidant capacities.

Bee products exhibit varying antioxidant capacities that serve as natural buffers against oxidative stress, analogous to capacity planning in systems where reserves are strategically allocated to handle disruptions.  
Higher antioxidant capacity in certain honeys and propolis enables better cellular protection and resilience, mirroring how well-planned resource buffers improve system stability under load.  
Comparative analysis reveals that antioxidant strength is not uniform, highlighting the importance of selecting the right “resource type” for specific environmental demands in capacity planning.  
This understanding supports optimized usage strategies, much like matching capacity investments to anticipated operational stressors for maximum efficiency and longevity.

A comparative study of relational learning capacity in honeybees and stingless bees.

Relational learning capacity differs significantly between honeybees and stingless bees, demonstrating how different species allocate cognitive resources for environmental adaptation.  
Honeybees generally show superior relational learning, reflecting a higher investment in flexible problem-solving capacity suited to complex foraging environments.  
This variation illustrates that cognitive capacity planning in biological systems is shaped by ecological niche and evolutionary pressures.  
Understanding these differences informs bio-inspired models for designing adaptive capacity in artificial systems facing variable task demands.

Botanical Origin of Galician Bee Pollen for the Characterization of Phenolic Content and Antioxidant Activity.

Botanical origin strongly determines the phenolic content and antioxidant activity of bee pollen, directly influencing its protective capacity against oxidative damage.  
Pollen from diverse floral sources creates a natural portfolio of antioxidant capacities, similar to diversified capacity planning that mitigates risk through variety.  
Strategic collection from multiple botanical origins enhances overall functional capacity and resilience of the hive’s resource base.  
This natural diversification strategy offers valuable lessons for building robust, multi-source capacity systems in engineering and supply chain management.

Use of an innovative T-tube maze assay to assess sublethal effects on learning capacity of the honey bee.

The T-tube maze assay effectively measures sublethal impacts of stressors on honeybee learning capacity, serving as a sensitive indicator of cognitive resource depletion.  
Reduced learning performance under chemical exposure reveals how external factors can constrain cognitive capacity planning at the individual and colony level.  
This approach enables early detection of capacity erosion before overt behavioral collapse occurs.  
It underscores the need for proactive monitoring and protective measures to preserve essential learning capacity in complex adaptive systems.

Botanical Origin, Phytochemical Profile, and Antioxidant Activity of Bee Pollen from the Mila Region, Algeria.

Botanical origin shapes the phytochemical profile and antioxidant activity of bee pollen, determining its functional capacity as a natural protective resource.  
Regional floral diversity creates distinct antioxidant signatures that enhance the colony’s resilience to environmental stress.  
This variation demonstrates how source diversity directly impacts overall system capacity and defensive capability.  
Such findings support the principle that strategic sourcing and diversification are key to building high-quality, resilient capacity in both natural and engineered systems.

Genotypic trade-off between appetitive and aversive capacities in honeybees.

Genotypic trade-offs exist between appetitive (reward-seeking) and aversive (risk-avoidance) learning capacities in honeybees, showing that cognitive resources are finite and competitively allocated.  
Certain genotypes prioritize strong appetitive learning at the expense of aversive learning, revealing inherent constraints in cognitive capacity planning.  
This trade-off illustrates that biological systems must strategically balance different types of learning capacity based on environmental demands.  
Understanding these trade-offs is valuable for designing balanced capacity architectures in artificial intelligence and organizational systems.

Assessment of Bioactive Compounds under Simulated Gastrointestinal Digestion of Bee Pollen and Bee Bread: Bioaccessibility and Antioxidant Activity.

Simulated gastrointestinal digestion reveals the bioaccessibility and retained antioxidant activity of bee pollen and bee bread, demonstrating how processing affects functional capacity.  
Only a portion of bioactive compounds remains available after digestion, highlighting the importance of evaluating real-world capacity rather than nominal content.  
This assessment shows that bee products maintain significant protective capacity even after digestive processing, supporting their role as effective natural buffers.

text:
OK, after some intense usage of GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, and GLM 5.2, here are my thoughts:

1️⃣GPT 5.5 is the one you can trust most of the time. It has its quirks—like being overly defensive and prone to over-engineering—but these can be largely mitigated with good prompt engineering. However, I feel its review capability is lagging; Opus 4.8 handles this better. GPT 5.5 also gets incredibly stubborn and sticks to its guns even when it's wrong. The best way to snap it out of it is to ask it to prove its claim using pure logic or a reproduction test. Even then, it will occasionally throw in a defensive "but" 😂, though this approach works most of the time. Additionally, it tends to drop instructions after a few messages (which could be due to tool calls consuming the context window).

2️⃣Opus 4.8 is a solid model for reviewing and planning large tasks. It occasionally misses tiny details, but it's generally dependable. Its review capabilities are the strongest among the three; even when bringing its code review skills over to Codex, GPT 5.5 just couldn't catch up. It also follows instructions literally most of the time. If your documentation is outdated due to a recent code change, it will explicitly point it out and let you choose how to proceed—really solid behavior. When it does get something wrong, a few quick questions will get it back on track, unlike GPT 5.5, which drags you into an argument.

3️⃣GLM 5.2 is a really impressive model for pure execution. You can generate a plan using GPT and Opus, hand it to GLM for implementation, and it will handle a massive PR incredibly well with only a few minor omissions. The best way to snap it out of it is to ask it to prove its claim using pure logic or a reproduction test. Even then, it will occasionally throw in a defensive "but" 😂, though this approach works most of the time. Additionally, it tends to drop instructions after a few messages (which could be due to tool calls consuming the context window).

2️⃣Opus 4.8 is a solid model for reviewing and planning large tasks. It occasionally misses tiny details, but it's generally dependable. Its review capabilities are the strongest among the three; even when bringing its code review skills over to Codex, GPT 5.5 just couldn't catch up. It also follows instructions literally most of the time. If your documentation is outdated due to a recent code change, it will explicitly point it out and let you choose how to proceed—really solid behavior. When it does get something wrong, a few quick questions will get it back on track, unlike GPT 5.5, which drags you into an argument.

America’s standard of living has been in decline for decades.

There is a group of respected intellectuals — Charles Murray, Nicholas Eberstadt, Robert Putnam, and to some degree J.D. Vance — who paint the story of America’s decline as a failure of culture. In these narratives, we are in trouble because we abandoned the habits of thrift, work, and family formation. As a consequence, America’s families and economic lives are falling apart. The failure is in the souls of Americans, and the remedy is a moral reconstruction.

I have enormous respect for these writers. I think they are describing, with real precision, the sociological texture of what has happened. But I know they have the causation backward.

In America’s ongoing decline, the social scientists are adept at measuring the obvious signs of distress: drug addiction, gambling, prostitution, suicide. But these problems did not destroy our culture. These problems are a result of what has been destroying our country. And that is hard for them to measure because they are not looking at the economics behind these changes.

A culture of thrift does not survive a monetary regime that punishes savers.
A culture of marriage does not survive an economy in which young men cannot afford to form households.
A culture of work does not survive a labor market in which working-class wages have tracked sideways for 50 years while asset prices have gone to the moon.

The cultural problems — the lack of thrift, the abandonment of marriage, and chronic underemployment — are rational responses to our current economic environment. When the economy ceases to reward traditional male roles, the culture adjusts. 

You can see this clearly if you look at the exceptions. 

In every demographic slice of America where the Cantillon transfer has been positive — where the households in question have been recipients of the new money, not victims of it — the old cultural patterns are completely intact.

Upper-middle-class professionals in Bethesda still marry at high rates. They still form stable families. They still raise their children with discipline, invest in their education, attend their kids’ sporting events, and stay married into their seventies.

They did not suffer a cultural collapse, because they did not suffer an economic collapse.

It is the people who did not receive the new money whose culture has come apart. And that is not a coincidence. That is the causation.

If you want to rebuild America’s culture, you have to first rebuild the currency.

“Where the fuck have you been?!” my wife was crying

“I’m sorry, my phone died and Hassan said I should sleep over…”

“Hassan?! Your 43 year old driving instructor?!” my wife screamed

“Yes, but he got me an Uber in the morning…”

It was absolutely disgusting

How could she get into an unlicensed taxi?

This could have ended terribly. She could have been hit with surge pricing and paid €13 for what should be an €8 ride

I filed the complaint with the EU transport authority before she sobered up

I hope my daughter will never make this mistake again

text:
Achieving massive scalability on Ethereum L1 — around 10,000 transactions per second — would have enormous implications for what blockchains can realistically do.

That is about 864 million transactions per day. At that scale, Ethereum would no longer be limited to niche crypto apps or high-value settlement between other systems. It could start handling the normal economic activity of large consumer platforms.

That does not mean every part of a global app would run onchain. Videos, feeds, etc would still mostly run off-chain.

But the important parts of apps that decide who gets paid, who owns the account, who has a contract, who has a reputation, and who can take their business elsewhere could move onto Ethereum.

For example, with a YouTube or TikTok-scale creator platform, the videos would still be hosted offchain, and the feed would still be managed by an app, but the creator's income could go directly into their own wallet. Their paid subscribers could be connected to them onchain. Their membership payments, tips and revenue shares would not just be entries in one company's private database.

A platform could still remove them from its own app, but it could not seize their balance, delete their paying audience, or cut off their ability to get paid by anyone else.

Think an onchain version of Uber or Upwork: the app could still match drivers with riders or freelancers with clients. But the payment, deposit, work contract and reputation could live outside the app:

A driver with 10,000 completed rides would not have to leave that history behind if they moved to another marketplace, and a freelancer's work record would not be trapped inside one company's database.

A client could put money into escrow, the worker could complete the job, and payment could settle automatically without either side needing to trust the platform as much.

Or consider stablecoin payments at the scale of national payment networks.

A worker could get paid in dollars without needing a bank account.

If you wanted to start accepting payments on your own website, you would not need to apply for a merchant account with a credit card processor.

Anyone could open a small online business and start receiving global payments with almost no friction.

That means fewer barriers to commerce. More people can sell. More people can work. More people can get paid. More people can build businesses without asking a bank, platform or payment processor for permission first.

The result of all of this would be a less siloed economy: more open, more efficient and more competitive, with fewer monopolistic gatekeepers controlling entire markets from the top.

And as those benefits compound over time, the result should be a much more prosperous society.

quotedTweet.text:
Ethereum has spent the last several years scaling without taking the easy shortcut of turning the base chain into a datacenter chain.

Since 2020, the major upgrades have been:

• Beacon Chain: introduced Proof of Stake.
• The Merge: completed the transition from Proof of Work to Proof of Stake, laying the groundwork for data sharding to enhance rollup scalability.
• EIP-4844 (Proto-Danksharding): introduced data blobs, enabling massive scaling of rollup solutions by significantly reducing data availability costs through the use of KZG polynomial commitments to enable Ethereum to verify that blob data without putting that data permanently into L1 calldata. Raised rollup scalability to 650 transactions per second (TPS).
• Pectra: doubled target blob throughput per block, from 3 to 6, with the maximum rising from 6 to 9. This raised rollup capacity to roughly 980 TPS.
• Fusaka: introduced PeerDAS, so nodes no longer need to download every piece of blob data in full. They can sample the data instead, using erasure coding to efficiently reconstruct the full data. This is the first real stage of data sharding.
• Blob Parameter Only forks: lets Ethereum keep increasing blob capacity without waiting for a full hard fork. The first two BPO increases raised Ethereum to 14 blobs, with a maximum of 21. That raised maximum rollup capacity to 2,300 TPS.

At the same time, Ethereum's L1 gas limit has been raised to around 60M, or 238 TPS, from 45 TPS in 2020.

The next major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is aimed at making much higher L1 capacity safe through ePBS, block-level access lists, and parallel execution. It will also continue blob scaling for rollups. 

The post-Glamsterdam target is 200M gas limit, or 790 TPS on Mainnet.

The long-term roadmap has also expanded, with Ethereum now working toward bringing ZK verification directly into mainnet. That means using ZK proofs of EVM execution to raise throughput without forcing every validator to run much more powerful hardware. This is about Ethereum L1 itself becoming ZK-verifiable.

The long-term goal is around 10,000 transactions per second on Ethereum mainnet, with rollups scaling to 10M TPS. So gigagas L1 and a much larger rollup data layer, while still preserving the property that makes Ethereum ultra-hard: ordinary people being able to verify the chain.

text:
地球的最优人口其实只有25亿，但全球人口已超80亿。当印度、巴基斯坦、尼日利亚等国人口严重超载，爆发饥荒与高温时，大规模的移民潮就变成了一场无声的战争。

大批外来移民正在疯狂挤占英、美、加、澳以及中国香港等地的生存资源，导致这些发达地区的生活水平肉眼可见地倒退。这本质上是一场零和博弈：多一个移民，就可能挤死一个当地人。所有国家迟早要面临选择——让自己的国民死，还是让移民死？

西方之所以出现这种悲剧，核心在于选票政治——政客为了选票去收买、优待移民。如果不加以控制，未来全球必然集体右转，甚至会重现集中营和强制遣返等极端手段。

对于中国来说，最明智的策略就是严防死守，绝不接受任何移民。

同时，最有效的防御手段就是彻底切断选票绑架：

只发劳工签证：对特定高风险地区的移民永远不给国籍，只发一年一签、可随时驱逐的劳工签证，不给任何政治权利。
取消政治资格：即使已入籍的特定族裔，也必须剥夺其选举与任职资格。

只要移民没有了选票价值，政客就不会放任其涌入。在残酷的生存资源争夺战面前，守住边界，才是对自己国民最大的负责。

text:
Karpathy 说了一句反常识的话：用自然语言写 prompt 让 AI 写代码，其实效率很低。

他的做法是直接把光标移到要改的位置，敲前3个字母，让模型自动补全。光标位置+上下文代码+前几个字符，信息密度比你打一段英文描述高得多。

他把 AI 编程分了三档：完全不用（过时了）、vibe coding 全交给 AI（大部分场景不靠谱）、自己当架构师 AI 当补全工具（他选这个）。

为什么不信 vibe coding？他拿自己的项目举了个例子：8张GPU同步梯度他没用标准的 DDP，自己写了一套。AI 反复逼他改回 DDP，完全理解不了为什么有人不用标准方案。

模型的问题不是不够聪明，是"记忆太多"。训练数据里全是标准写法，你一写非标准的东西它就懵了，还会偷偷把你的代码往"常见写法"上改。

有一个大佬朋友，早年是牛逼闪闪的企业家，现在退出江湖，隐居在美国深宅大院。

早年与结发妻子生有一子，早已长大成人，名校博士毕业，投行工作，事业有成；

后遇见年轻漂亮明眸善睐的现任，又生两子，现在美国陪伴孩子成长，不亦乐乎！

在西方，有钱人大多离婚再娶，在中国，更倾向于三妻四妾纳外室。

传统道德更多的约束普通人，亿万美元身家或权倾朝野的人，社会似乎更加包容他们的言行及生活方式。

有两个身在中国的同龄中产朋友，都有三个孩子，天伦之乐肯定有了，但也是养育孩子压力不小，但如果资产再增加十倍呢，或许做父亲的压力反而更小。

父亲节略有感悟，你想要做一个怎样的父亲？想要成为几个孩子的父亲？
